newsitem.title: USA: Marathon sees 372,000 BOE/day output in 97.
newsitem.headline: Marathon sees 372,000 BOE/day output in 97.

text.p: Marathon Oil Co expects 1997 output will be 372,000 barrels per day of oil equivalent this year, President Victor Beghini said Thursday.
Going forward, he told PaineWebber's annual energy conference, several factors point to continued growth for Marathon.

-- Four deepwater fields are scheduled to come on stream in the Gulf of Mexico by 1999, more than doubling Gulf liquids production, compared to 1996. He said this will put liquids at 65,000 barrels per day, adding natural gas output would rise 35 percent to 120 million cubic feet a day.
-- The West Brae/Sedgwick subsea project is expected to attain first oil in late 1997 in the U.K. North Sea.
-- Marathon has taken 28 percent interest in the Poseidon crude oil pipeline and 24.33 percent in the Nautilus natural gas pipeline being built -- both to serve Gulf deepwater growth.
-- Added-value capital programs being completed this year include a gas oil hydrotreater at the Garyville, Louisiana, refinery and crude-unit expansion at the Robinson, Illinois, refinery.

"With the completion of projects in progress, liquids production volumes are expected to rise by 35,000 barrels per day from 1996 to 1999, reaching a level of 216,000 barrels per day -- the highest in 10 years and 20 percent above last year," Beghini said.
Worldwide gas sales are expected to remain relatively steady, averaging about 1.25 billion cubic feet per day over that span.
Neither forecast assumes any additions from new discoveries or acquisitions, he noted.
Strategic opportunities for expansion are plentiful for Marathon across the board, he indicated.
"Upstream, we retain a selective focus on low-cost reserve targets -- as in the Gulf of Mexico and Cotton Valley. Both areas have a large number of prospects that offer excellent opportunities."

Downstream, Beghini said, "we see opportunities in pipeline transportation systems, adding value through managing refining assets, and growing the Marathon Brand independent operator network and Emro company-operated retail network to expand sales volumes and total margins."
